subproblem.title: Deformation theorem for integer multiplicity currents with a finite set of approximating currents (Simon Ch. 6, 5.1–5.4)
subproblem.statement: For all P, m ∈ ℕ (degree n := m + 1) there is a constant c ∈ ℝ≥0 with c ≥ 1 such that for every ρ > 0, every compact K ⊆ ℝ^P and every Λ ∈ ℝ≥0 there is a finite set 𝒬 of currents in 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) with the following property. If T ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) is integer multiplicity, spt T ⊆ K, M(T) ≤ Λ and M(∂T) < ∞, then there are Q ∈ 𝒬, R ∈ 𝒟_{n+1}(ℝ^P) and S ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) such that: Q, ∂Q and R are integer multiplicity; T − Q − S = ∂R; Q = 0 or M(Q) ≥ ρⁿ; M(Q) ≤ c·M(T), M(∂Q) ≤ c·M(∂T), M(R) ≤ c·ρ·M(T) and M(S) ≤ c·ρ·M(∂T); spt Q ∪ spt R ⊆ thickening(3√P·ρ, spt T) and spt ∂Q ∪ spt S ⊆ thickening(3√P·ρ, spt ∂T), where thickening(r, A) := {x : |x − y| < r for some y ∈ A} (Mathlib Metric.thickening; it is empty when A = ∅). Here M := massOn ℝ^P is the total mass (GeometricCurrentOn.mass, with the Euclidean coefficient norm), masses and products are read in [0, ∞], and spt is the support of Simon 6.2.11 (GeometricCurrentOn.support). Nothing beyond these properties is asserted about Q: in particular the statement does not assert that Q is a polyhedral chain (that is only a feature of the construction used in the proof).

subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 6, §5 (Deformation Theorem 5.1, scaled version 5.3, Lemma 5.4 and the proof (1)–(38), chapter-06.txt lines 1405–1928, printed pp. 158–168), with the tools it cites: homotopy formula and mass estimate 2.25–2.29 (lines 440–530), slicing 4.6–4.10, integrality of push-forwards 3.3–3.9, completeness 3.13 and the BV facts 2.34–2.37 and Ch. 2, 2.7, 2.9 used on the faces. Where Simon cites a result whose proof is not in the pinned library, the argument is given below (Parts A–C); the main proof (Parts D–E) is Simon's printed proof with details filled in. Departures: (i) Simon's 3.13 (completeness) is replaced by the direct integral representation of the push-forwards (B3–B4), which shows integrality without passing to limits of integer multiplicity currents; (ii) the BV structure of the face densities (Simon's appeal to 2.35 and Ch. 2, 2.7, 2.9) is replaced by the integer multiplicity structure of Q plus the elementary Poincaré and trace inequalities of C1–C2; (iii) the printed constant “|y − a| ≥ 3/4” in the proof of 5.4 is corrected to |y − a| ≥ 1/4 (a ∈ B_{1/4}(q), y ∈ ∂C), which only changes constants; (iv) the support radius 2√P ρ of the statement is used in the slightly weaker form 3√P ρ (the face-replacement step (E7) moves supports by up to √n ρ more), which is what the Lean statement asserts. Scope of the statement: the conclusion asserts only that Q lies in the finite set 𝒬 and has the listed integrality, mass and support properties. That the Q constructed below is a polyhedral chain Σ_F β_F[[F]] on the cubical grid of side ρ with integer coefficients β_F is a property of this construction; it is used inside the proof (E0) to define the finite set 𝒬 and to obtain the dichotomy Q = 0 or M(Q) ≥ ρⁿ, and it is not part of the conclusion.

Notation and conventions. n := m + 1 ≥ 1 is the degree. IM := integer multiplicity (contract IsIntegerMultiplicity). All currents in this proof live in ℝ^P (domain univ) or ℝ × ℝ^P; M(X) := M_{ℝ^P}(X) = X.mass; |α| is the Euclidean coefficient norm of a covector, |ω|_∞ := sup_x |ω(x)|; for a k-vector ζ (continuous linear functional on k-covectors) |ζ| := sup{⟨α, ζ⟩ : |α| ≤ 1} (dual norm). For currents X, Y, X + Y := X − (0 − Y). The zero current (in any degree) is IM: the IMRep with empty carrier, multiplicity 0 and orientation 0 represents the zero current (∅ is Borel and countably rectifiable by SimonGMT countablyRectifiable_of_measure_zero; the positivity, integrability, measurability and orientation fields hold vacuously because μHE restricted to ∅ is the zero measure; and the representing integral over ∅ is 0); this is used whenever Q, R or S is taken to be 0. Siblings used: vanish_off_support (VO), mass_equals_rep_measure (MR), mass_representation (REP: representation (μ_X, ξ_X) with μ_X(G) = M_G(X), |ξ_X(x)(α)| ≤ |α|, and absolute continuity μ_X ≪ Hᵏ for X with M + M∂ locally finite), im_calculus (IMC: locality of approximate tangent spaces, IM restrictions, differences), slicing (SL). For X with compact support and finite mass, (VO) and (REP) give μ_X(ℝ^P ∖ spt X) = 0, so μ_X is a finite measure with compact support, and |X(ω)| ≤ ∫ |ω| dμ_X. For a Borel set B and a bounded Borel g, X⌞B(ω) := ∫_B ξ_X(ω) dμ_X and X⌞g(ω) := ∫ g ξ_X(ω) dμ_X are currents (linear; sequentially continuous because |X⌞g(ω)| ≤ sup|g|·|ω|_∞·μ_X(tsupport ω)) with M(X⌞g) ≤ ∫ |g| dμ_X, and X⌞g(ω) = X(gω) for smooth g; for IM X these agree with the IM restrictions of IMC(b) (both represent the same vector measure on test forms, hence on bounded Borel functions).

Multilinear algebra used throughout (Euclidean norms).
(L0) For a k-covector β on ℝ^P, k!|β|² = Σ_{i_1,…,i_k} β(e_{i_1}, …, e_{i_k})² =: ‖β‖²_HS (alternating: each increasing tuple appears k! times up to sign, tuples with repeats vanish). ‖·‖_HS is invariant under orthogonal changes of basis (it is the Hilbert–Schmidt norm of the multilinear form), hence so is |·|; and the dual norm on k-vectors is invariant as well.
(L1) For a linear map A : ℝ^P → ℝ^Q and a k-covector β on ℝ^Q, |A^#β| ≤ ‖A‖^k |β|; dually |Λ_k A ζ| ≤ ‖A‖^k |ζ| for k-vectors ζ, where ⟨β, Λ_kAζ⟩ := ⟨A^#β, ζ⟩. Proof: by (L0) it suffices to bound ‖·‖_HS; replacing one slot of a multilinear form γ by A multiplies its Hilbert–Schmidt norm by at most ‖A‖ (for fixed other arguments, Σ_i γ(Ae_i, …)² = |Aᵀg|² ≤ ‖A‖²|g|², g the vector representing γ(·, …)); do this k times.
(L2) For a 1-covector β' and a k-covector γ, |β' ∧ γ| ≤ |β'||γ|: by (L0) rotate so that β' = |β'|e¹; then β' ∧ γ = |β'| Σ_{I∌1} γ_I e¹ ∧ e^I. Dually |v ∧ ζ| ≤ |v||ζ| for a vector v and a k-vector ζ, where ⟨β, v ∧ ζ⟩ := ⟨ι_vβ, ζ⟩ (and |ι_vβ| ≤ |v||β| likewise).
(L3) If τ_1, …, τ_k are orthonormal then ζ := τ_1 ∧ ⋯ ∧ τ_k (⟨α, ζ⟩ := α(τ_1, …, τ_k)) has |ζ| = 1 (by (L0) rotate so that τ_i = e_i; then ⟨α, ζ⟩ = α(e_1, …, e_k) is one coordinate of α). If A : ℝ^k → ℝ^P is linear and injective, write A = O S (polar decomposition: S := (AᵀA)^{1/2}, O := AS⁻¹ an isometric embedding); then Λ_kA(e_1 ∧ ⋯ ∧ e_k) = det(S)·Oe_1 ∧ ⋯ ∧ Oe_k, so |Λ_kA(e_1 ∧ ⋯ ∧ e_k)| = det S = √det(AᵀA) =: JA and Λ_kA(e)/JA is a unit simple k-vector orienting A(ℝ^k); if A is not injective, Λ_kA(e) = 0 = JA. Two unit simple k-vectors orienting the same k-plane differ by a sign (change of orthonormal basis has determinant ±1). Also, by IMC(d), the orientation of an IMRep satisfies |⟨α, ξ⟩| ≤ |α| a.e.

Part A. Calculus of normal currents with compact support.
A1 (Smooth push-forward; Simon 2.23–2.24.) Let X ∈ 𝒟_k(ℝ^P) have compact support and F : ℝ^P → ℝ^Q be C^∞. For ω ∈ 𝒟^k(ℝ^Q) let (F^#ω)(x)(v_1, …, v_k) := ω(F(x))(DF(x)v_1, …, DF(x)v_k) (Lean: (ω (F x)).compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ F x)), a smooth k-form, and F_#X(ω) := X(ζ F^#ω) with ζ ∈ C_c^∞(ℝ^P) equal to 1 near spt X; by (VO) this does not depend on ζ. F_#X is a current (if ω_j → 0 in 𝒟^k(ℝ^Q) then ζF^#ω_j → 0 in 𝒟^k(ℝ^P) by the chain and Leibniz rules), ∂F_#X = F_#∂X (d commutes with F^# — SimonGMT Chapter06 exteriorDerivativeOn_pullbackFormWithin — and X(dζ ∧ F^#ω) = 0 by (VO)), and spt F_#X ⊆ F(spt X). If M(X) < ∞, then F_#X(ω) = ∫ ⟨ω(F(x)), Λ_k DF(x) ξ_X(x)⟩ dμ_X(x), so by (L1) M(F_#X) ≤ ∫ ‖DF‖^k dμ_X ≤ sup_{spt X} ‖DF‖^k M(X).
A2 (Product with [[0,1]]; Simon 2.17–2.21.) Write points of ℝ × ℝ^P as (t, x) and e₀ := ∂_t. For an (k+1)-form ω on ℝ × ℝ^P let ω₁(t, x) be the k-covector on ℝ^P given by ω₁(t,x)(v_1, …, v_k) := ω(t,x)(e₀, (0,v_1), …, (0,v_k)) and ω₀ the “dt-free part”. For X ∈ 𝒟_k(ℝ^P) with compact support define ([[0,1]] × X)(ω) := X(∫_0^1 ω₁(t, ·) dt) (the integrand is a smooth compactly supported k-form on ℝ^P), and ({s} × X)(ω) := X(i_s^#ω), i_s(x) := (s, x). These are currents in ℝ × ℝ^P with compact support. Writing ω = dt ∧ ω₁ + ω₀, d(dt ∧ ω₁) = −dt ∧ d_xω₁ and dω₀ = dt ∧ ∂_tω₀ + d_xω₀, so (dω)₁ = ∂_tω₀ − d_xω₁; integrating in t and using that d_x commutes with ∫dt gives
 ∂([[0,1]] × X) = {1} × X − {0} × X − [[0,1]] × ∂X (for k ≥ 1; for k = 0 the last term is absent).
If M(X) < ∞ then ([[0,1]] × X)(ω) = ∫_0^1 ∫ ⟨ω(t,x), e₀ ∧ ξ_X(x)⟩ dμ_X dt and M([[0,1]] × X) ≤ M(X).
A3 (Homotopy formula and estimate; Simon 2.25–2.27.) For C^∞ maps F, G : ℝ^P → ℝ^Q let H(t, x) := F(x) + t(G(x) − F(x)). Since ∂H_# = H_#∂ and H ∘ i_1 = G, H ∘ i_0 = F, A2 gives
 G_#X − F_#X = ∂H_#([[0,1]] × X) + H_#([[0,1]] × ∂X) (last term absent for k = 0).
If M(X) < ∞: DH(t,x)e₀ = G(x) − F(x) and DH(t,x)(0, v) = ((1 − t)DF(x) + tDG(x))v, so Λ_{k+1}DH(e₀ ∧ ζ) = (G − F)(x) ∧ Λ_k((1−t)DF + tDG)(x)ζ and by (L1), (L2)
 M(H_#([[0,1]] × X)) ≤ ∫ |G − F| (‖DF‖ + ‖DG‖)^k dμ_X ≤ sup_{spt X}|G − F| · sup_{spt X}(‖DF‖ + ‖DG‖)^k · M(X).
A4 (Lipschitz push-forward; Simon 2.29.) Let X have compact support with M(X) + M(∂X) < ∞ (k ≥ 1; for k = 0 drop the ∂X terms) and F : ℝ^P → ℝ^Q be Lipschitz with constant Λ. F_σ := F ∗ φ_σ (componentwise mollification) is C^∞, ‖DF_σ‖ ≤ Λ, F_σ → F uniformly. By A3 for F_σ, F_τ,
 |(F_σ)_#X(ω) − (F_τ)_#X(ω)| ≤ sup|F_σ − F_τ| ((2Λ)^k M(X)|dω|_∞ + (2Λ)^{k−1}M(∂X)|ω|_∞) → 0,
so F_#X(ω) := lim_{σ↓0}(F_σ)_#X(ω) exists. Properties: (a) |F_#X(ω)| ≤ Λ^k M(X)|ω|_∞, so F_#X is a current and M(F_#X) ≤ Λ^k M(X); (b) ∂F_#X = F_#∂X; (c) for smooth F it agrees with A1 (DF_σ → DF uniformly on compact sets); (d) spt F_#X ⊆ F(spt X) (if spt ω ∩ F(spt X) = ∅ then spt ω ∩ F_σ(spt X) = ∅ for small σ); (e) if F, G are Lipschitz (constants ≤ Λ) and |F − G| ≤ δ on spt X, then |F_#X(ω) − G_#X(ω)| ≤ δ((2Λ)^k M(X)|dω|_∞ + (2Λ)^{k−1}M(∂X)|ω|_∞) (pass to the limit in A3); in particular F_#X depends only on F|spt X, so for a map ψ that is Lipschitz on a closed set A ⊇ spt X, ψ_#X := (ψ̃)_#X is well defined for any Lipschitz extension ψ̃ of ψ|A (componentwise McShane extension, Mathlib LipschitzOnWith.extend_real, constant ≤ √Q Lip(ψ|A)), and linear in X among currents supported in A; (f) homotopy formula: for Lipschitz F, G, with H(t,x) := F(x) + t(G(x) − F(x)) (Lipschitz on [0,1] × ℝ^P when G − F is bounded, extended to t ∉ [0,1] by clamping), G_#X − F_#X = ∂H_#([[0,1]] × X) + H_#([[0,1]] × ∂X) and M(H_#([[0,1]] × X)) ≤ sup_{spt X}|G − F|·(Lip F + Lip G)^k M(X), similarly for ∂X with exponent k − 1 (apply A3 to F_σ, G_σ with the homotopies H_σ(t, x) := F_σ(x) + s(t)(G_σ − F_σ)(x), where s ∈ C^∞(ℝ) is bounded with s(t) = t on [−1, 2] (only [0,1] × spt X matters, so A3 holds verbatim with s in place of t); the H_σ are globally Lipschitz with bounded constants and converge uniformly to H(t, x) := F(x) + s(t)(G − F)(x), so by (e) applied in ℝ × ℝ^P and lower semicontinuity of mass, SimonGMT WeaklyConvergesOn.massOn_le_liminf, the identity and the estimate pass to the limit).

Part B. Integrality of Lipschitz push-forwards (Simon 3.3–3.9 and 3.2(2)).
Throughout X = τ(M, θ, ξ) is an IM k-current in ℝ^P (k ≥ 1) with compact support and M(∂X) < ∞; by (MR) and (IMC) we may assume M ⊆ spt X, so Hᵏ(M) ≤ ∫_M θ dHᵏ = M(X) < ∞. Lebesgue measure on ℝᵏ is Lᵏ, Hᵏ = μHE[k].
B1 (Parametrization.) There are countably many compact sets A_i ⊆ ℝᵏ, Lipschitz G_i : ℝᵏ → ℝ^P and κ_i > 0 such that: G_i is differentiable at every u ∈ A_i with DG_i(u) injective; |G_i(u) − G_i(v)| ≥ κ_i|u − v| for u, v ∈ A_i; the sets G_i(A_i) ⊆ M are pairwise disjoint; Hᵏ(M ∖ ⋃_i G_i(A_i)) = 0. Moreover, given an open set O with Hᵏ(M ∖ O) = 0 and a countable family of compact sets whose interiors cover O, the construction may be run on M ∩ O, so that Hᵏ(M ∖ ⋃_i G_i(A_i)) = 0 still holds and each G_i(A_i) lies inside one member of the family.
Proof. By definition (SimonGMT CountablyRectifiable) M ⊆ M₀ ∪ ⋃_j F_j(ℝᵏ) with Hᵏ(M₀) = 0 and F_j Lipschitz. By Rademacher (Mathlib LipschitzWith.ae_differentiableAt) the set D_j of differentiability points of F_j is Borel with null complement, and Hᵏ(F_j(ℝᵏ ∖ D_j)) = 0 (Lipschitz images of null sets are null, Mathlib LipschitzOnWith.hausdorffMeasure_image_le). On Z_j := {u ∈ D_j : DF_j(u) not injective} the Jacobian vanishes, so Hᵏ(F_j(Z_j)) = 0 (SimonGMT Chapter02 area_image_criticalSet_eq_zero). Let E_j := (D_j ∖ Z_j) ∩ F_j^{-1}(M) (Borel). For injective A choose an antilipschitz constant K_A > 0 (Mathlib LinearMap.exists_antilipschitzWith: |Au| ≥ |u|/K_A) and put r(A) := 1/(2K_A); r(A) := 1 for non-injective A. Apply Mathlib exists_partition_approximatesLinearOn_of_hasFDerivWithinAt to F_j on E_j with this r: E_j is covered by disjoint Borel sets E_j ∩ t_l on which F_j approximates A_l = DF_j(y_l) (injective, y_l ∈ E_j) with constant r(A_l), i.e. |F_j(u) − F_j(v) − A_l(u − v)| ≤ r(A_l)|u − v|; hence |F_j(u) − F_j(v)| ≥ |A_l(u − v)| − r(A_l)|u − v| ≥ (2K_{A_l})⁻¹|u − v| there, so F_j is injective and bi-Lipschitz on E_j ∩ t_l. Enumerate all pieces as (E_i, G_i, κ_i), intersect with the compact members of the given cover (pulled back), and make the images disjoint inductively, E'_i := E_i ∖ G_i^{-1}(⋃_{i'<i} G_{i'}(E'_{i'})); images of Borel sets under continuous maps injective on them are Borel (Mathlib MeasurableSet.image_of_continuousOn_injOn), so the E'_i are Borel.
